evidence.note: Claim: a generic ratchet over git ls-files reading [quality].max_file_bytes catches a new oversized file and a grown baselined file. Falsifier: tests/test_file_size_ratchet.py::test_an_oversized_new_file_fails_the_ratchet fails to flag a temp 30010-byte file. Ran: pytest tests/test_file_size_ratchet.py -> errored first (no Config.quality), then 6 passed after wiring.
r-small-files, r-everything-configurable (limit is the knob), r-reuse-core (G.files reused), r-tell-dont-discover (note names the split action and the list)

chunk_findings.detail: `violations` treats an empty `oversized` result as proof that no Python file is over the limit, but `oversized` returns `{}` whenever the check is disabled (`limit <= 0`) or when git could not list files. Given the repository baseline is present and `violations(repo, 0)` is called, `over` is `{}` while `base` still contains the baseline entries, so the `set(base) - set(over)` loop appends “... is no longer over 0 bytes: delete its line ...” for every baselined file. Thus setting `[quality].max_file_bytes` to 0 (the documented off value) makes the ratchet fail, and a git-listing failure produces false baseline-stale violations instead of no result or a distinct error.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/file_size.py:63 (`violations`)

chunk_findings.detail: The stated conformance requires per-area constants that mean the same thing as `[quality].max_file_bytes` to be replaced, but the manifest for this change contains no edit to `tests/test_config_layout.py` (or the other layout tests) where `MAX_MODULE_CHARS = 30000` still exists. With an org lock such as `[quality].max_file_bytes = 20000`, the new ratchet rejects a 25000-byte module, while `test_config_layout.py` still permits up to 30000 characters, leaving a hardcoded duplicate cap and violating [r-everything-configurable]/[r-small-files]. The added architecture note only excuses `MAX_*_LINES` caps, not the character cap.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_config_layout.py:MAX_MODULE_CHARS

chunk_findings.detail: The baseline is explicitly declared shrink-only and says “never add a line,” but this line adds an exemption for `ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py` whose own reason says the file “crossed the limit after the baseline was first measured.” That is a newly oversized file being grandfathered. Given `ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py` at 30393 bytes and `[quality].max_file_bytes` 30000, `FS.violations` should report a new oversized file; because the baseline line exists, `test_no_new_oversized_file_and_no_baselined_file_grew` passes instead, violating the intent’s “fails a new oversized file” and “baseline … only shrinks.”
chunk_findings.title: tests/guard_baselines/file_size_baseline.txt:18

chunk_findings.detail: The intent requires `[quality].max_file_bytes` to be added with “org lock”, but the `knob(...)` definition passes only `doc` and `check`. It does not declare `lock`/`org_lock` or an equivalent org-policy lock property, so the knob is not registered as org-lockable. An organization setting this limit in shared org config could have a local clone override it (for example `max_file_bytes = 0` to turn the check off), defeating the `r-small-files` ratchet the change is meant to enforce.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/quality.py:QualityConfig.max_file_bytes

chunk_findings.detail: `violations` does not honor the “check is off” case that `oversized` explicitly implements for `limit <= 0`. Given a repo with the non-empty default baseline and `[quality].max_file_bytes = 0`, `oversized` returns `{}`, but `violations` still reads the baseline and loops over `set(base) - set(over)`, appending “is no longer over 0 bytes: delete its line” for every baseline entry. The ratchet would then fail even though the limit knob is set to disable the check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/file_size.py:violations

chunk_findings.detail: The baseline has 14 exempt entries, not the 11 stated in the intent. The last entry exempts `ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py` at 30393 bytes and its own reason says it “crossed the limit after the baseline was first measured.” That is a newly over-limit source file added to the shrink-only baseline, so `FS.violations(ROOT, LIMIT)` will pass the current repo even though a source file exceeds `[quality].max_file_bytes`. This defeats the new-file ratchet and violates the file’s own header “never add a line.”
chunk_findings.title: tests/guard_baselines/file_size_baseline.txt:18

chunk_findings.detail: `LIMIT` is captured once from `Config().quality.max_file_bytes`, and `test_default_limit_is_30k` hardcodes 30000. In a supported org-locked configuration that sets `[quality].max_file_bytes` to a non-default value such as 40000, importing the test makes `LIMIT = 40000` and the assertion `LIMIT == 30000` fails; the remaining ratchet tests then use the wrong limit.
